hero.caption: Looking west from Fox Covert Lane across the fields of Fenn Lane Farm (the farm is left, on the skyline). Fen Hole is approximately where the hedge line in the foreground is.  The cortege carrying Richard III's remains visited the farm and soil was taken and placed in the king's grave when he was re-buried in Leicester Cathedral in 2015. The fields on either side of Fenn Lanes Roman road correspond to the flat plain which William Burton (writing in the early 1600s) described as the site of the battle: "fought in a large, flat, plaine, and spacious ground, three miles distant from [Bosworth], between the Towne of Shenton, Sutton [Cheney], Dadlington and Stoke [Golding]..," It was in the fields to either side of Fenn Lanes (the route of approach of Richmond's army) that the Battlefields Trust found the round shot and silver-gilt boar badge, identifying the true site of the battle. (Ambion Hill was the site of Richard III's camp, not the site of the battle).

images.filename: The actual site of the Battle of Bosworth^ - geograph.org.uk - 675443.jpg
images.caption:
The actual site of the Battle of Bosworth? This footpath starts here at Foxcovert Lane, crosses over Fenn Lanes, and carries on to the small Leicestershire village of Upton. 
A recent archaeological survey and archaeological finds in this area has revealed that these fields mark the actual site of the Battle of Bosworth. Ambion Hill and the current visitor centre lie over a mile across fields to the north-east. There are plans to link the two sites via a footpath.

images.filename: The death of Richard III at Bosworth.jpg
images.caption:
An image from a set of 8 extra-illustrated volumes of A tour in Wales by Thomas Pennant (1726-1798) that chronicle the three journeys he made through Wales between 1773 and 1776. These volumes are unique because they were compiled for Pennant's own library at Downing. This edition was produced in 1781.
The volumes include a number of original drawings by Moses Griffiths, Ingleby and other well known artists of the period.
